INTELLIGENT MACHINES - PART 3

Interactive purchasing workspace

Single-tray-indexing food assembly line with three robot arms: Arm 1 places three varieties of cheese, Arm 2 places crackers, and Arm 3 places apple slices. An operator replenishes ingredient presentation trays and grapes are placed manually. Trays are denested onto a conveyor; assembled product undergoes vision inspection, followed by manual lid closure and sealing, and exits as a sealed tray. The diagram explicitly excludes a grape picker and lid applicator. Estimated throughput is approximately 135 acceptable plates/hour, compared with 240/hour in the original design; customer approval is required for the lower throughput and extended production window. A replenishment operator and a closure/sealing operator are illustrated, but total staffing and assignment of manual grape placement are not specified.

Human decision required. This page does not authorize purchases. Unknown or weakly supported facts remain qualification gaps.
6 core process purchases
5 supporting items
11 total requirements covered

Input architecture

The purchasing agent preserves this process design; it does not redesign the line.

Confirmed assumptions

Packaging SpecificationsUse the same tray and lid format assumed in Part 2; exact dimensions, materials, tolerances, nesting details, and plate-to-tray relationship remain unresolved and require samples before purchase.
Product And Portion SpecificationsUse the same ingredient list and portions modeled in Part 2: three cheese varieties, crackers, apple slices, and manually placed grapes. Exact dimensions, weights, temperatures, surface conditions, and acceptable damage limits require product samples and trials.
Throughput And StaffingPlanning case is approximately 135 acceptable trays per hour using a 22-second modeled bottleneck, 2-second index time, and 90% effectiveness. The longer production window and operator staffing for replenishment, grapes, and closure are not customer-approved.
Food Contact And SanitationAny direct-food-contact component must be food safe. Cleaning method, chemicals, allergen-changeover procedure, and documentation requirements remain unresolved.
Operating EnvironmentUse the Part 2 refrigerated planning range of 36-40 F. Humidity, condensation, exposed-food hold-time, and exact ambient conditions require confirmation.
UtilitiesUnknown; obtain site electrical, compressed-air, vacuum, network, and any sealing-utility requirements before purchase.
Closure And SealingThe diagram specifies manual lid closure and sealing with no automatic lid applicator. Exact lid geometry, snap-fit or seal mechanism, seal-integrity criteria, and need for an operator-actuated device remain unresolved.
Vision AcceptanceInspection should check assembly completeness before closure. Defect classes, accuracy, false-accept and false-reject limits, and failed-product handling remain unresolved.
Layout And SafetySingle-tray indexed flow with three robot arms and human access for replenishment, grape placement, and closure. Footprint, working height, guarding, safety zoning, and detailed operator access require an integrator risk assessment.
Jurisdiction And CertificationsUnknown; installation jurisdiction, machinery and electrical requirements, food-contact documentation, hygienic-design expectations, and customer-specific certifications are blocking qualification questions.

Integration and qualification requirements

  • Controls, station interfaces, and safeguarding require integrator design.
  • Food-contact materials, sanitation method, cold operation, and applicable ingress ratings require configuration-specific evidence.
  • Representative product and packaging trials must confirm handling, inspection, closure, and throughput.
  • Site utilities and jurisdiction-specific certifications remain human approval gates.

Core equipment implements the process stations. Supporting equipment covers loading, accepted-product handoff, and reject/rework handling. Linked specifications are supplier claims, not independent certification.

Open decisions

Show detailed human decisions from the sourcing run
  • Approve sample trials and final purchasing only after food-contact, sanitation and robotic-picking acceptance.
  • Approve approximately 135 acceptable trays/hour, the extended production window and staffing for replenishment, manual grapes and manual closure/sealing.
  • Approve presentation capacity, mounting and any separately qualified fixtures without changing the confirmed line architecture.
  • Authorize any procurement overbuy separately; case quantities do not change the required operating quantity of one tray per requirement.
  • Approve actual product samples, tray footprint, usable capacity and operator/robot interfaces.
  • Approve food-contact documentation, sanitation procedure, refrigerated holding conditions and jurisdiction-specific requirements.
  • Approve reduced throughput, extended production window and staffing for replenishment, grapes and closure.
  • Confirm supplier quotation and delivery commitment; final purchasing remains a human decision.
  • Approve tray samples, single-tray pitch, station spacing, operator access, and a guarded layout before ordering.
  • Approve robot reach and cycle simulations, guarding, and food trials before selecting any arm or end effector.
  • Run apple end-effector trials and a vision feasibility study using real assembled trays before purchase.
  • Approve tray/lid specifications, sealing method and acceptance tests before selecting sealing equipment.
  • Approve sanitation, jurisdictional requirements, layout and operator safety.
  • Approve the approximately 135 acceptable trays/hour planning case, extended production window and staffing, including manual grapes.
  • Make the final purchasing decision after sample trials and a confirmed supplier quotation.
